title: Proof of categorical mass markov
html:
Proof

The chain has three steps:

Step 1 (Categorical trace \to Frobenius integral). The categorical trace \mathrm{tr}(f) = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_{A^\vee}) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A descends under the fibre functor \tau to the Frobenius integral \int_A : A \to R—the Jones–Markov trace on H_n(R, q) (RJ interpretation), satisfying Markov properties I and II (vertex algebra relations, QU-3).

Step 2 (Nakayama automorphism = identity). The mass involves \Psi = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta, the Nakayama automorphism of the Frobenius algebra A. For Frobenius–Hopf algebras, \Psi = S^2. In H_n(R, q) the antipode S(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i^{-1} yields S^2(\sigma_i) = \sigma_i, hence \Psi = \mathrm{id}_A.

Step 3 (Mass = trace of cycle). Substituting \Psi = \mathrm{id}:

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}
  \;=\; \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    \underbrace{(\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta}_{= \,\mathrm{id}_A}
    \circ\, \varrho \bigr) \bigr\rVert
  \;=\; \Bigl|\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})\Bigr|.

Explicit values

Evaluating at q_0 \approx 1.110 with Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) \approx 0.613 (convention D, SU(2)/Temperley–Lieb — see the trace-convention registry) and h = q - q^{-1} \approx 0.209:

The convention-C column has no producer by design: C was excised by the owner ruling of 2026-08-09, so nothing in the repo computes it and no witness can carry it. The convention-D column is witnessed by computations/markov/markov-trace-canonical.witness.json (6 assertions at 10^{-40}) — the script this note already names below as the reproducer, which until now emitted no witness at all (bean qou-ft3p).

h is convention-independent. The 4_1 closed form is new here: it was "(see witness)", and the witness held the C value. Reproduce with python3 computations/markov/markov_trace_canonical.py, whose prop-table check now gates at 10^{-40} rather than 10^{-9}.

These constitute dimensionless ratios relative to the photon (\mathfrak{m}_{q,\gamma} = 1). Physical masses in MeV require a calibration constant E_0, determined by anchoring to one experimental value (e.g., the free neutron \beta-decay Q-value).

Role in the unified mass formula

This proposition supplies the k = 0 stratum of the curvature-rank decomposition (unified mass formula): \mathfrak{m}^{(0)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(1) = |\!\int_A\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K})| is the descended Frobenius integral, equal to E_\infty^{0,*} of the GB spectral sequence.

The integral \int_A \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}) is vortex-specific, distinguishing \varrho_{\mathfrak{p}} from \varrho_{\mathfrak{n}} and capturing fine isotope variations. The vortex-independent constant offset is the Frobenius co-Casimir m_e \cdot \tau(C_{\dim_q}) (Frobenius universal). The full mass is:

  \mathfrak{m}_{q,\mathcal{K}}
  \;=\; \sum_{k \geq 0} \alpha_k \cdot \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(1)
       \;+\; m_e \cdot \tau(C_{\dim_q}),

with this proposition governing the k = 0 component.
